one_line_idea: Generators have seen the benchmarks: synthetic training data leaks evaluation content through generator memorization, inflating synthetic-data results in ways standard contamination checks never audit.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Text-to-image generators are trained on web-scale corpora that overlap with the sources of vision benchmarks, and synthetic-data experiments treat generated images as contamination-free because their pixels are new.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Prompting generators in the semantic vicinity of benchmark content produces training images that leak test-set-specific information (near-duplicate compositions, distinctive instances), measurably inflating benchmark scores of models trained on such synthetic data.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] A leakage audit will find benchmark-adjacent generations at nonzero rates under natural prompting, and students trained with leak-heavy versus leak-scrubbed synthetic data will show score differences on the affected benchmarks but not on fresh evaluation data.
why_important: Synthetic data is being adopted partly to escape contamination concerns; demonstrating a laundering pathway through the generator would change evaluation hygiene requirements across the field.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Generator memorization is established; its quantified downstream effect on benchmark inflation via synthetic training data may be unaudited.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Generate synthetic training data with natural task prompts, run near-duplicate retrieval against benchmark test splits, scrub matches, train students on scrubbed versus unscrubbed data, and compare benchmark versus fresh-data performance.
main_risk: Semantic near-duplicate detection has threshold ambiguity, and the leak rate may vary enormously across benchmarks and prompting styles.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Generated images are assumed contamination-free because they are not copies of any real file.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Memorization means the generator can emit information about specific training items, and benchmarks live in that training set; novelty of pixels is irrelevant to information leakage.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Prompt one generator with class names of one benchmark and retrieve nearest test-set neighbors; visible near-duplicates in an afternoon establish the pathway.

judge_A_meta.judge_notes: WAVE1 FLAG: wave1 family C-023/C-064 (contamination); generator-memorization leakage channel is the new mechanism.

one_line_idea: Reported synthetic-data gains are confounded by asymmetric tuning effort, and equal-tuning-budget re-evaluation would deflate a measurable share of published improvements.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Papers proposing synthetic-data pipelines tune generation parameters, mixing ratios, and training recipes for their method, while baselines are typically run at default or lightly tuned settings, a pattern documented in other subfields as a source of inflated gains.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Under matched hyperparameter search budgets for both arms, a substantial fraction of published synthetic-data improvements shrinks or disappears, and the surviving gains identify the subset of techniques with real effect.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Re-evaluating a sample of published synthetic-data results with symmetric tuning protocols will reduce the median reported gain noticeably, with shrinkage correlating with the original paper's baseline-tuning opacity.
why_important: Meta-corrections of this kind have repeatedly recalibrated subfields; synthetic data is due for one before its conclusions are cemented into industrial practice.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Equal-tuning audits exist in other areas; a systematic one for synthetic-data claims may not.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Select representative published synthetic-data results with available code, define a symmetric tuning budget, re-run both arms, and report the gain-shrinkage distribution.
main_risk: Reproduction fidelity disputes are inevitable, and the audit needs preregistered protocols to be credible.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Published synthetic-data gains are taken at face value as method effects rather than tuning-asymmetry effects.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Synthetic pipelines add many new tunable degrees of freedom, and every added degree of freedom is an opportunity for asymmetric optimization to masquerade as improvement.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Take one prominent result, give the baseline the same tuning budget the pipeline received, and measure the surviving gain in a handful of runs.

judge_A_meta.judge_notes: WAVE1 FLAG: wave1 family C-045 (hidden budgets); tuning-effort asymmetry in the synthetic-data literature is the substrate.

one_line_idea: Per-image accounting hides the cost of synthetic data: under per-FLOP accounting that includes generation compute, many synthetic-data results are net-negative versus simply training longer on real data.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Synthetic-data comparisons equalize image counts or training steps while excluding the substantial compute spent generating the images, so the reported comparisons answer a question no budget-constrained practitioner actually faces.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] When total compute (generation plus training) is the equalized resource, the synthetic-data advantage shrinks systematically, and for a meaningful class of settings the same compute spent on longer real-data training or stronger augmentation wins outright.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Re-running representative synthetic-augmentation setups under total-compute matching will flip a nontrivial fraction of positive results to neutral or negative, with the flips concentrated where generation cost per image is high relative to training cost.
why_important: Compute is the actual constraint in practice; accounting that ignores the generation bill systematically overstates synthetic data's practical value and misleads infrastructure decisions.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Cost caveats appear in discussions; a systematic total-compute-matched re-evaluation of synthetic-data claims may be unpublished.
minimal_falsification_experiment: For several synthetic-augmentation settings, measure generation FLOPs, construct total-compute-matched real-only baselines (longer schedules, heavier augmentation, larger models), and compare outcomes at equal total budgets.
main_risk: Generation cost is amortizable across many downstream uses, so single-use accounting may be unfair to synthetic data in multi-project organizations.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Synthetic data comparisons at matched image counts are accepted as the standard fair protocol.
why_it_might_be_wrong: An intervention that costs compute must be benchmarked against other uses of that compute, and per-image protocols exempt synthetic data from exactly that comparison.
fastest_falsification_experiment: For one published-style setup, give the real-only baseline extra training equal to the measured generation compute and see whether the synthetic advantage survives; two runs plus bookkeeping.

judge_A_meta.judge_notes: Kept: distinct falsifiable hypothesis after cross-shard dedup vs D+E+F and collision check vs the 248 wave-1 accepted ideas; novelty NOT verified (hypothesis-level dedup only, prior-art search pending).

one_line_idea: Batch-generated synthetic data violates the i.i.d. assumption through shared seeds, prompts, and scheduler state, and decorrelating generation batches yields free training gains.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Training theory and practice assume approximately independent samples, while synthetic data is produced in correlated batches (shared prompt templates, sequential seeds, common guidance settings) whose within-batch similarity is never audited.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Within-batch correlation in generated data reduces the effective sample size and injects correlated gradient noise, so generation protocols that enforce cross-batch decorrelation (seed spacing, prompt interleaving, setting jitter) improve downstream training at identical image counts.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Measuring within-batch versus across-batch feature similarity will show substantial excess correlation under default generation, and students trained on decorrelated generations will outperform students trained on default generations at matched counts, with the gap growing at smaller dataset sizes.
why_important: This is a zero-cost protocol fix at generation time; if effective sample size is being silently wasted, every generative data pipeline is leaving performance on the table.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Correlation structure of generated corpora seems unexamined as a training-relevant property with a protocol-level remedy.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Generate matched corpora under default and decorrelated protocols from the same generator, quantify correlation structure in a fixed feature space, train matched students, and compare performance across dataset sizes.
main_risk: Decorrelation knobs may also change marginal image quality, requiring quality-matched controls to isolate the correlation effect.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Generated images are implicitly treated as independent draws from the generator's distribution regardless of how the sampling loop was executed.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Samplers are deterministic functions of highly structured inputs, and reusing structure across a batch mathematically cannot produce independent outputs.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Compute within-batch versus across-batch embedding similarity for one default generation run; excess within-batch similarity is measurable in hours and gates the training experiment.

judge_A_meta.judge_notes: Kept: distinct falsifiable hypothesis after cross-shard dedup vs D+E+F and collision check vs the 248 wave-1 accepted ideas; novelty NOT verified (hypothesis-level dedup only, prior-art search pending).

judge_C_meta.anomaly_note: Batch-generation i.i.d. violation via shared seeds/prompts/scheduler state is an overlooked statistical mechanism with a free mitigation.

one_line_idea: Renderer labels are not ground truth for the evaluation convention: anti-aliased boundaries, transparency, and reflections are labeled by renderer logic that systematically disagrees with human annotation guidelines.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Synthetic labels are generated by renderer visibility logic (which surface owns a pixel), while human annotation guidelines resolve mixed pixels, transparent surfaces, and reflections by task-specific conventions; the two resolution rules are never reconciled.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Renderer label conventions disagree with annotation guidelines on a systematic pixel population (boundaries, glass, mirrors, thin structures), and this disagreement imposes a measurable ceiling on synthetic-trained model performance under human-convention evaluation.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] An audit comparing renderer labels against guideline-compliant human annotation of the same synthetic frames will find concentrated systematic disagreement on the predicted pixel populations, and convention-corrected synthetic labels will lift real-benchmark performance of synthetic-trained models on those populations.
why_important: The assumption that rendered labels are perfect is foundational to the entire synthetic-data enterprise; quantifying where it fails defines the true label-quality budget of simulation.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Individual issues like transparency labeling are known irritations; a systematic renderer-versus-guideline disagreement audit with downstream impact measurement may be missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Have annotators label sampled synthetic frames under a real benchmark's guidelines, quantify disagreement with renderer labels by pixel population, then train with corrected labels and measure the recovered performance.
main_risk: Human annotation of synthetic frames imports human noise, so disagreement must be separated into systematic convention differences and ordinary annotator variance.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Rendered labels are called ground truth without qualification, and label error is assumed to be an exclusively real-data problem.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Visibility logic and human convention are different functions that provably diverge on optically complex pixels, and dense metrics integrate over exactly those pixels.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Inspect renderer labels on glass, mirrors, and thin structures for one synthetic dataset against the target benchmark's written guidelines; cataloguing systematic divergences takes one afternoon.

judge_C_adversary.reason: Renderer-logic labels disagreeing with human annotation guidelines (anti-aliasing, transparency, reflections) is the mechanism inventory behind F-027's convention-matching claim; one convention audit.

judge_A_meta.judge_notes: Kept: distinct falsifiable hypothesis after cross-shard dedup vs D+E+F and collision check vs the 248 wave-1 accepted ideas; novelty NOT verified (hypothesis-level dedup only, prior-art search pending).

one_line_idea: More realism is not monotonically better: past a threshold, realistic synthesis re-imports the real world's spurious correlations that cruder randomized data had removed, hurting robustness.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Real datasets contain spurious correlations (context-object coupling, texture shortcuts) that harm robustness, and low-realism randomized synthetic data breaks many of them by construction, while the community pursues maximal realism as an unquestioned goal.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Part of synthetic data's value is inadvertent bias removal, so as synthesis approaches full realism it restores the real distribution's shortcuts, producing a non-monotone robustness curve where intermediate randomization outperforms maximal realism on out-of-distribution evaluation.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Sweeping realism-versus-randomization while evaluating both in-distribution and shift-robustness metrics will show in-distribution performance rising with realism while robustness peaks at intermediate randomization, with the divergence traceable to reinstated context and texture shortcuts.
why_important: The realism-maximizing roadmap that guides simulation investment may be optimizing in-distribution scores at the direct expense of the robustness synthetic data was supposed to provide.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Randomization-for-invariance is known; the framing of realism as shortcut-restoration with a measured non-monotonicity may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Construct a realism ladder where known spurious correlations of the target domain are measurably present or broken per rung, train matched models per rung, and evaluate in-distribution accuracy alongside shortcut-sensitivity probes and shift robustness.
main_risk: Quantifying shortcut presence in training data requires committing to specific shortcut hypotheses, which may miss the correlations that actually matter.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The asymptote of synthetic data quality is assumed to be indistinguishability from real data, full stop.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Matching the real distribution exactly means matching its biases exactly, so a synthesis pipeline that can control bias is strictly more valuable than one that reproduces it faithfully.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Compare context-shortcut sensitivity (objects on unusual backgrounds) between models trained on randomized-context versus realistic-context synthetic data in two runs.

judge_A_meta.judge_notes: ANOMALY: Non-monotone realism: maximal realism re-imports the real world's spurious correlations that cruder randomization had removed.

judge_C_meta.anomaly_note: Realism re-importing the real world's spurious correlations past a threshold is the anti-thesis of the realism-helps default and of naive domain randomization. Protected tension.

one_line_idea: Synthetic data optimized to match today's distribution is optimized for the wrong target when deployment shifts the distribution, and shift-anticipating synthesis beats distribution-matching synthesis.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Synthetic data pipelines take the current real distribution as the matching target, while deployed systems face distributions altered by time, adaptation of users, and the system's own feedback effects.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For deployments with predictable shift structure (seasonal cycles, hardware upgrades, behavior adaptation), synthesizing data for plausible future distributions rather than the present one yields better performance over the deployment window, and the advantage is largest where retraining cadence is slow.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] In settings with documented temporal shift, models trained with shift-anticipating synthetic mixtures will outperform distribution-matched ones on later time slices while conceding little on the training-time slice, measured over held-out temporal sequences.
why_important: Matching the present is an unexamined default; if anticipation wins under realistic shift, the target-selection step becomes a first-class design decision in every synthetic pipeline.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Temporal robustness is studied for models; using synthesis specifically to pre-train for forecast distributions may be unexplored.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Use datasets with timestamped sequences exhibiting real drift, build present-matched and forecast-matched synthetic augmentations, train matched models, and evaluate across subsequent time slices.
main_risk: Forecasting distribution shift is itself hard, and a wrong forecast could underperform the present-matching default, making the method's value contingent on forecast quality.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The real distribution at collection time is treated as the definitionally correct synthesis target.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Training data determines performance during deployment, not during collection, and the two distributions demonstrably differ in any system that operates over time.
fastest_falsification_experiment: On one dataset with known seasonal structure, compare present-matched versus season-shifted synthetic augmentation for a model evaluated on the next season's data; two runs decide the direction.

judge_A_meta.judge_notes: Kept: distinct falsifiable hypothesis after cross-shard dedup vs D+E+F and collision check vs the 248 wave-1 accepted ideas; novelty NOT verified (hypothesis-level dedup only, prior-art search pending).

one_line_idea: Synthetic data is assumed privacy-safe by construction, but generator memorization leaks training individuals, and the utility cost of verified non-memorization is unknown and possibly severe.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Synthetic data is marketed as a privacy solution because generated records are not copies of real ones, while generative models demonstrably memorize and can reproduce near-copies of training samples under some conditions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For visual data containing people and identifiable scenes, the achievable frontier between measured re-identification risk and downstream utility is materially worse than assumed, and enforcing verified non-memorization (filtering or training constraints) costs a quantifiable, possibly large, share of the synthetic data's utility.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Mapping the risk-utility frontier by varying memorization-mitigation strength will show utility declining substantially before re-identification risk reaches levels that privacy claims imply, and unmitigated pipelines will exhibit nonzero measurable leakage.
why_important: Institutions are adopting synthetic data specifically for privacy compliance; an unmeasured risk-utility frontier means those decisions rest on an assumption rather than a measurement.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Memorization and privacy are studied separately; a utility-annotated frontier for vision synthetic-data pipelines may be missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: For one generator trained on identifiable visual data, sweep mitigation strength, measure leakage with membership-inference and near-duplicate retrieval, train students per setting, and plot the joint risk-utility frontier.
main_risk: Leakage measurement methods have their own blind spots, and a clean-looking frontier could reflect weak auditing rather than actual safety.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Generated data is treated as anonymized by default because no real record appears verbatim.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Privacy is about information flow, not file identity, and memorization is precisely an information flow from training individuals to generated outputs.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Run near-duplicate retrieval from a generator's outputs back into its known training set at scale; nonzero verified matches establish the leak before any frontier mapping.

judge_A_meta.judge_notes: Kept: distinct falsifiable hypothesis after cross-shard dedup vs D+E+F and collision check vs the 248 wave-1 accepted ideas; novelty NOT verified (hypothesis-level dedup only, prior-art search pending).

judge_C_meta.anomaly_note: Privacy leakage through generator memorization in 'privacy-safe by construction' synthetic data, and the unknown utility cost of verified non-memorization.

one_line_idea: The domain gap is treated as a scalar when it is a decomposable vector over appearance, content, sensor, and label-convention factors, and interventions are systematically misattributed as a result.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Papers report a single sim-to-real gap number and attribute its reduction to their intervention, though the gap aggregates several mechanistically distinct mismatch factors that different interventions address.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A factor-wise decomposition protocol (controlled swaps of appearance, content statistics, sensor pipeline, and label convention between synthetic and real) yields stable, additive-enough gap components, and re-analyzing standard interventions against components reveals widespread misattribution of their effects.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Component-wise measurement across dataset pairs will show interventions concentrating their effect on single components (translation on appearance, resampling on content), with published whole-gap narratives frequently crediting the wrong mechanism, and component profiles predicting intervention transfer across pairs.
why_important: A vector-valued gap converts sim-to-real research from anecdote comparison into mechanism accounting, letting practitioners diagnose before treating.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Individual factor studies exist; a standardized decomposition protocol with intervention re-attribution may not.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Build controlled swap experiments for one synthetic-real pair (relight and retexture for appearance, resample for content, ISP transplant for sensor, convention transform for labels), measure component gaps, and re-evaluate representative interventions component-wise.
main_risk: Components interact (appearance changes affect content perception), so additivity is approximate and the protocol needs interaction terms to stay honest.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The gap is one number, and any method that shrinks it is understood to have addressed the domain gap as such.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Distinct causal mechanisms cannot be diagnosed or treated through their sum, and every mature engineering field decomposes its error budgets.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Implement two swaps (sensor ISP transplant and label-convention transform) on one pair and check whether their measured components are non-trivial fractions of the whole gap.

judge_A_meta.judge_notes: Kept: distinct falsifiable hypothesis after cross-shard dedup vs D+E+F and collision check vs the 248 wave-1 accepted ideas; novelty NOT verified (hypothesis-level dedup only, prior-art search pending).

one_line_idea: Generation vintage is a hidden curriculum: synthetic corpora accumulate quality drift as pipelines improve, and ordering training by vintage versus shuffling changes outcomes, an unexamined degree of freedom.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Large synthetic corpora are accumulated over months of pipeline evolution (generator upgrades, prompt improvements, filter changes), producing systematic quality and distribution drift across the corpus that training treats as exchangeable data.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Vintage drift is large enough that sample order and vintage-conditioned weighting materially affect final models: shuffling hides a drift signal that could be exploited (curriculum from old to new, or downweighting obsolete vintages) or that silently harms reproducibility when ignored.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Auditing an accumulated corpus will reveal measurable vintage-correlated distribution shifts, and training runs differing only in vintage ordering or weighting will differ beyond seed noise, with newest-vintage-weighted training winning on current evaluations.
why_important: Organizations sit on accumulated synthetic corpora and assume exchangeability; a vintage effect changes both how to train on them and how to interpret historical experiments run at different corpus states.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Data-vintage effects are discussed for web crawls; the internal vintage structure of accumulated synthetic corpora may be unexamined.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Take a corpus with generation-time metadata, quantify vintage drift in a fixed feature space, and run matched trainings under shuffled, chronological, reverse-chronological, and vintage-weighted regimes.
main_risk: Vintage correlates with content changes made deliberately (new prompt themes), so drift must be separated into pipeline drift and intentional content evolution.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] A synthetic corpus is treated as a bag of exchangeable samples regardless of when and how each sample was produced.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Every pipeline change moves the generated distribution, and months of accumulated changes cannot leave the corpus exchangeable; the only question is whether training is sensitive to it.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Embed samples from the oldest and newest vintage of one accumulated corpus and measure their separability with a simple classifier; strong separability confirms the premise in hours.

judge_C_adversary.reason: Generation-vintage quality drift as hidden curriculum and crawl-vintage synthetic contamination drift are one vintage-effects program; one vintage-stratified training study.

judge_A_meta.judge_notes: Kept: distinct falsifiable hypothesis after cross-shard dedup vs D+E+F and collision check vs the 248 wave-1 accepted ideas; novelty NOT verified (hypothesis-level dedup only, prior-art search pending).

one_line_idea: The student-cannot-exceed-teacher assumption fails for dense geometry: averaging noisy generator-derived labels across many views or samples lets students surpass their labeling teacher measurably.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Auto-labeling pipelines assume the student's accuracy is bounded by the teacher's, and dense geometric labels (depth, correspondence) derived from teachers are noisy per-sample, while multiple correlated estimates per scene point are often available across views and samples.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] When teacher errors are partly independent across views, augmentations, or samples of the same underlying geometry, aggregate supervision (multi-view consistency fusing many noisy teacher estimates) carries more information than any single teacher output, letting students exceed teacher accuracy in a predictable regime defined by error correlation.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Students trained on consistency-fused teacher labels will exceed the teacher's own accuracy on held-out real geometry benchmarks, with the exceedance margin tracking the measured independence of teacher errors across views, and vanishing when errors are fully correlated.
why_important: This identifies the exact condition under which auto-labeling escapes the distillation ceiling, turning a folklore impossibility into an engineering criterion for label-fusion pipeline design.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Multi-view fusion and distillation are both standard; framing and measuring teacher-exceedance as a function of error-correlation structure in dense labeling may be new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Use a teacher to produce per-view depth estimates over multi-view real scenes, fuse them with geometric consistency, train a student on fused labels, and compare student versus teacher accuracy on independent ground truth, alongside measured cross-view error correlation.
main_risk: Teacher errors are often systematically shared across views (textureless regions), which caps the achievable exceedance and may confine the effect to favorable scene types.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] A student trained on a teacher's outputs is assumed to be at best a compressed copy, never more accurate than its supervision source.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Averaging partially independent noisy measurements provably reduces error, and geometry provides the consistency constraints that turn many bad labels into one good one.
fastest_falsification_experiment: On scenes with available ground truth, compare raw teacher depth against multi-view-fused teacher depth; if fusion already beats the raw teacher, the information headroom for the student is established without training.

judge_A_meta.judge_notes: ANOMALY: Students exceed teachers via multi-view consistency fusion — a predictable exceedance regime defined by teacher-error independence.

judge_C_meta.anomaly_note: Students exceeding the labeling teacher for dense geometry via multi-view/sample averaging is the anti-thesis of F-052's ceiling. Protected tension.

one_line_idea: Real and synthetic data follow different scaling exponents that interact, and a two-term joint scaling law fitted from pilot runs predicts the optimal real-synthetic mix at any budget.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Scaling laws are fitted for single-source corpora, while practitioners face two-source budget decisions (how much real, how much synthetic) with no quantitative model of how the sources combine.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Real-data volume, synthetic-data volume, and their interaction determine loss through a stable parametric surface (task-dependent exponents plus a substitution term), fittable from small pilot grids and extrapolable to larger budgets with useful accuracy.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Joint scaling fits from pilot-scale grids will predict held-out large-budget mixed-training outcomes within tolerances that make mix-selection reliable, and the fitted substitution elasticity between real and synthetic data will vary systematically by task type.
why_important: A validated mixing law converts synthetic-data budgeting from sweep-based guesswork into a forecastable engineering computation, at exactly the scales where sweeps are unaffordable.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Data-mixing scaling work exists for language corpora; a validated real-synthetic joint law for vision tasks with substitution-elasticity interpretation may be missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Run a pilot grid over real and synthetic volumes for several tasks, fit candidate two-source laws, and validate extrapolation against held-out larger-budget runs including the predicted optimal mixes.
main_risk: Synthetic data quality is heterogeneous, and a law fitted for one generator configuration may not transfer to another without refitting.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Mixing decisions are assumed to require empirical sweeps at the target scale because the sources interact unpredictably.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Scaling regularity has held across every data regime where it has been carefully measured, and two-source training is a modest extension of measured territory.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Fit the law on a small grid for one task and test its prediction at one point outside the grid; a week of small runs establishes whether the functional form holds.

judge_A_meta.judge_notes: Kept: distinct falsifiable hypothesis after cross-shard dedup vs D+E+F and collision check vs the 248 wave-1 accepted ideas; novelty NOT verified (hypothesis-level dedup only, prior-art search pending).

one_line_idea: Synthetic-data returns plateau when the student saturates the generator's effective support, and the intrinsic dimension of the generated set predicts the plateau point before training reaches it.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Adding synthetic data shows diminishing returns at some scale, but the plateau point is discovered empirically per project, with no predictive quantity that anticipates where more generation stops paying.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The plateau occurs when training has consumed the generator's effective support (the data manifold it can actually produce), so support-size measures (intrinsic dimension estimates, coverage growth curves of generated sets) predict the saturation scale independently of the student's architecture.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Across generators of different diversity, the synthetic-data scale at which student improvement plateaus will correlate strongly with measured effective-support statistics of the generated corpus, and truncation interventions that shrink support will shift the plateau earlier by the predicted amount.
why_important: A pre-training plateau predictor tells teams when to stop paying for generation and switch budget to real collection or generator improvement, a recurring high-stakes decision.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Diminishing returns are universally observed; a validated support-based predictor of the saturation scale may not exist.
minimal_falsification_experiment: For several generator configurations with measurable support statistics, train students across a data-scale ladder, locate plateaus, and test the support-statistic correlation plus the truncation-shift prediction.
main_risk: Intrinsic-dimension estimators are notoriously sensitive to feature space and scale choices, and a fragile estimator would produce an unfalsifiable moving target.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Diminishing returns are attributed loosely to data quality limits, with the plateau treated as an empirical surprise each time.
why_it_might_be_wrong: A student cannot keep learning from a source that has no more distinct content to show, so saturation must be governed by some measure of the source's content capacity.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Compare plateau points of one student trained on a truncation-limited versus a full-diversity variant of the same generator; the ordering is checkable with two data ladders.

judge_C_adversary.reason: Intrinsic-dimension plateau prediction and generator within-class recall ceiling are two operationalizations of one hypothesis: generated-set effective diversity bounds student gains.

one_line_idea: The true unit cost of synthetic data is dominated by curation, validation, and integration rather than generation, and total-cost accounting reverses several published cost-benefit claims.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Synthetic data is promoted as cheap because per-image generation cost is low and falling, while the surrounding pipeline (filtering, label verification, convention alignment, dataset QA, mixing experiments) consumes engineering effort that no paper accounts for.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Under honest total-cost-of-ownership accounting across real projects, the generation step is a minority of synthetic-data cost, and for a class of tasks the all-in cost per unit of performance gained exceeds that of straightforward real-data collection and annotation, reversing the headline economics.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Instrumented case studies tracking all pipeline costs will show curation-validation dominating generation cost by a substantial factor, and the resulting cost-per-performance comparisons will flip the synthetic-versus-real verdict in a measurable fraction of studied settings.
why_important: Organizational adoption decisions cite per-image cost; if the decision-relevant number is several times larger, many adoption decisions are being made on the wrong arithmetic.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Cost discussions exist qualitatively; instrumented total-cost case studies with performance-normalized comparison may be absent from the literature.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Run several matched projects (synthetic pipeline versus real collection) with full cost instrumentation and identical performance targets, and report all-in cost per achieved performance unit for each route.
main_risk: Cost structures vary across organizations and task types, limiting generality of any small set of case studies.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Synthetic data is assumed cheap because generation compute is cheap, with pipeline labor treated as negligible or one-time.
why_it_might_be_wrong: In every data modality studied carefully, cleaning and integration dominate acquisition; there is no reason generated data, which adds artifact auditing to the list, would be the exception.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Retrospectively cost-account one completed synthetic-data project from logs and invoices; a single honest ledger showing curation dominance justifies the systematic study.

judge_C_adversary.reason: Total-cost accounting (curation/validation/integration) and per-FLOP accounting including generation compute are one full-cost re-accounting audit that flips published cost-benefit claims.

one_line_idea: Small domain-specialized generators beat giant general generators as training-data engines at equal generation compute, contradicting the bigger-generator-is-better default.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Data-generation pipelines default to the largest available general-purpose generative model, paying its per-sample compute premium, while small generators fine-tuned on target-domain data are cheap to sample but presumed lower quality.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For a fixed generation-compute budget, a small domain-tuned generator produces more useful training data (more samples, better domain coverage, fewer irrelevant modes) than a large general model, except when the task requires compositional breadth only the large model has.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] At matched generation FLOPs, students trained on small-specialist output will outperform students trained on large-generalist output for in-domain tasks, with the ordering reversing on tasks demanding out-of-domain compositional variety.
why_important: Generator choice is the first and largest cost decision in every generative data pipeline, and the default choice may be systematically wasteful for the common case of narrow-domain applications.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Model-size tradeoffs are studied for generation quality; the compute-normalized comparison as training-data engines may be unmeasured.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Fine-tune a small generator on target-domain data, match total generation compute against a large general model, train identical students on each output, and compare on in-domain and breadth-demanding evaluations.
main_risk: The specialist's fine-tuning data requirement partially defeats the purpose in truly low-data domains, bounding the method's applicable regime.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The strongest available generator is assumed to produce the best training data, making generator scale a proxy for data quality.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Per-sample quality and per-FLOP data utility are different objectives, and sampling many adequate in-domain images plausibly beats sampling few excellent unfocused ones.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One domain, one small fine-tuned generator versus one large general model at matched sampling compute, two student runs; the in-domain ordering is immediately informative.

one_line_idea: When real data is exhausted, repeating real epochs beats adding synthetic data up to a predictable repetition count, and the repetition-versus-synthesis crossover is a fittable law.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] In data-constrained domains, practitioners choose between re-epoching limited real data and topping up with synthetic data, and the choice is currently made by intuition without a quantitative crossover model.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Marginal value of an additional real epoch decays predictably with repetition count while marginal value of synthetic additions is roughly constant but lower per sample, implying a computable crossover repetition count after which synthetic top-up wins, varying systematically with the domain gap of the synthetic source.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Sweeping repetition counts against synthetic top-up fractions in data-constrained settings will produce a stable crossover frontier, and the frontier location fitted at pilot scale will predict held-out larger-scale decisions within useful tolerance.
why_important: The repeat-or-synthesize decision arises in every data-limited project (medical, industrial, rare events), and a fitted rule would replace one of the most common ad hoc choices in applied vision.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Data-constrained scaling with repetition is characterized for language pretraining; a repetition-versus-synthesis crossover law for vision tasks may be unfitted.
minimal_falsification_experiment: In several data-constrained vision settings, grid over epochs-versus-synthetic-fraction at fixed compute, map the performance surface, fit the crossover frontier, and validate extrapolation at one larger scale.
main_risk: The crossover depends on synthetic quality, so the law needs a quality covariate to transfer across generators, complicating the fit.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Synthetic top-up is assumed helpful whenever real data is scarce, with repetition viewed as overfitting risk to be avoided.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Repetition of true samples re-presents unbiased evidence while synthetic additions present biased evidence, and the right mix must depend quantitatively on how fast repetition value decays versus how biased the synthetic source is.
fastest_falsification_experiment: At one small budget, compare four cells (low and high repetition, with and without synthetic top-up) to confirm the qualitative crossover exists before fitting any law.

judge_C_adversary.reason: Repeat-real-epochs-vs-add-synthetic crossover is a slice of F-097's joint scaling law (synthetic term vs repeated-real term); same fitted-law methodology.

one_line_idea: Synthetic datasets depreciate faster than real datasets as deployment distributions and conventions drift, and measuring dataset half-life reveals different amortization economics for the two data types.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Dataset value is treated as time-invariant in cost analyses, though both the world and pipeline conventions drift, and synthetic data additionally encodes generator-era artifacts and design assumptions that age with tooling.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Training value decays with dataset age for both data types, but synthetic datasets decay faster because they inherit era-specific generator artifacts, prompt fashions, and convention choices on top of world drift, giving them a measurably shorter half-life and worse amortized economics than per-image costs suggest.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Training current models on age-ladders of real and synthetic datasets for the same task will show steeper performance decay with age for synthetic sets, and the excess decay will be attributable to generator-era artifacts via artifact-normalization controls.
why_important: Amortization assumptions determine whether synthetic pipelines are investments or consumables; a shorter half-life changes procurement, retention, and regeneration policies for data-holding organizations.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Dataset aging is observed anecdotally; a comparative half-life measurement between real and synthetic data may not exist.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Assemble real and synthetic datasets of varying vintages for one stable task, train current models on each, evaluate on current real test data, and fit decay curves per data type with artifact-normalization ablations.
main_risk: Old synthetic datasets differ from new ones in many ways beyond age, so the ladder needs enough vintages and controls to separate aging from quality improvement.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] A dataset, once built, is treated as a durable asset whose training value persists until the task itself changes.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Synthetic data is a snapshot of both a world model and a tooling era, and two drift clocks tick faster than one.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Train one current model on an old versus a recent synthetic dataset for the same task and compare against the same-age contrast for real datasets; four runs bound the differential decay.

one_line_idea: The semantically strongest layer/timestep for diffusion-feature extraction is set by signal-to-noise ratio, not raw timestep index, and therefore transfers across models and noise schedules once re-parameterized in SNR.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Diffusion-feature papers report a per-model 'sweet spot' timestep and layer for semantic probes, and practitioners re-tune it for every new checkpoint and schedule.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Probe accuracy as a function of noise level collapses onto a single curve across models and schedules when indexed by log-SNR, because the denoising task difficulty (and hence the abstraction level of features) is determined by SNR alone.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] The log-SNR location of peak linear-probe accuracy will agree across at least three public diffusion checkpoints with different schedules to within 0.5 nats of log-SNR; kill the idea if the peak locations spread by more than 1.5 nats or if raw-timestep indexing aligns them equally well.
why_important: A schedule-invariant law would remove per-model tuning from every diffusion-as-backbone pipeline and would be direct evidence that feature abstraction is controlled by corruption level rather than architecture.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Sweet-spot timesteps are widely reported per model, but a cross-model SNR-collapse test with a pre-registered tolerance appears untested.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Extract U-Net/DiT features at 12 log-SNR levels from three public checkpoints with different schedules, train identical linear probes on a fixed classification/segmentation probe suite, and compare peak locations under SNR versus timestep indexing.
main_risk: Latent-space models change the effective data distribution the SNR acts on, so pixel-space and latent-space models may need separate SNR calibrations, weakening the universality claim.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Practitioners treat the optimal extraction timestep as a per-model hyperparameter without a governing law.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Architecture-specific inductive biases (attention density, resolution stages) may dominate over corruption level in deciding where semantics concentrate.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Feature extraction plus linear probes on a 10k-image public subset (ImageNet-scale classes) for three checkpoints is roughly one day on a single A100; no training of diffusion models required.

family_fingerprint.manipulated_variable: noise level indexing (SNR vs timestep) across checkpoints

one_line_idea: Dense correspondence ability in diffusion features lives in self-attention key/query geometry, not in convolutional value pathways, and the two can be dissociated by targeted feature surgery.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Diffusion features support zero-shot semantic correspondence, but which internal pathway carries the matching signal is not established; papers use whole-layer activations.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Correspondence accuracy is carried by the key/query token geometry of self-attention layers, while value/conv pathways mainly carry appearance; matching on key/query subspaces alone preserves correspondence while matching on value subspaces alone collapses it.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Key/query-only matching will retain at least 85% of full-feature correspondence accuracy (PCK) while value-only matching retains under 50%; kill the idea if the two subspaces are within 10 PCK points of each other.
why_important: Localizing the correspondence signal enables far cheaper correspondence extraction (a low-dimensional subspace) and tells us what generative pretraining actually learns about part identity.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Diffusion-correspondence papers ensemble layers; a controlled key/query-versus-value dissociation with pre-registered margins appears missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: On a standard public correspondence benchmark (e.g., SPair-71k), compute matches from key, query, value, and conv activations separately at the best noise level, with dimensionality matched by random projection, and compare PCK.
main_risk: Subspace disentanglement may be layer-dependent, producing a mixed answer that supports neither clean hypothesis.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The community treats 'diffusion features' as a monolithic representation whose correspondence power comes from generative training generally.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Value pathways may encode part-specific appearance that is exactly what matching needs, making attention geometry secondary.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Correspondence evaluation over ~1k image pairs with four feature variants runs in a few hours on one GPU using public checkpoints and public benchmarks.

family_fingerprint.manipulated_variable: feature subspace used for matching (key/query vs value/conv)

evidence_label.prior_work_basis: KNOWN PRIOR WORK (model recall, unverified): zero-shot correspondence from diffusion features is established; the pathway-dissociation claim is MODEL SPECULATION.

one_line_idea: v-prediction and x0-prediction models yield markedly better high-noise semantic features than epsilon-prediction models of matched quality, because their outputs remain image-like where epsilon targets are nearly pure noise.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Diffusion models are trained under different output parameterizations (epsilon, v, x0) chosen for sampling stability, and feature-extraction studies mostly ignore the parameterization as a variable.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] At low SNR the learning signal for epsilon-parameterized networks is dominated by noise regression, so their internal features degrade faster with noise level than v- or x0-parameterized networks trained on the same data.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] At log-SNR below -2, linear-probe accuracy of v-parameterized features will exceed epsilon-parameterized features by at least 5 accuracy points on a fixed probe suite with matched architectures and data; kill if the gap is under 2 points or reverses.
why_important: If parameterization controls feature usability, the perception community should prefer specific parameterizations when choosing generative backbones, and generative training objectives double as representation-learning knobs.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Parameterization is discussed for sample quality and stability; its causal effect on internal representation content appears unstudied.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train small diffusion models (CIFAR/ImageNet-64 scale) identical except for output parameterization, then run the SNR-indexed probe suite on internal features of each.
main_risk: At small scale the parameterizations may converge to near-identical internal solutions, leaving the question open for large models.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Parameterization is viewed as a numerically different but representationally equivalent reweighting of the same objective.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The equivalence arguments concern the training distribution-matching objective, not what intermediate layers must compute to satisfy it at each noise level.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two or three CIFAR-scale diffusion trainings (about 1 GPU-day each on a single consumer GPU) plus probing; total under 4 GPU-days with public data.

one_line_idea: Diffusion features encode intrinsic scene properties (albedo, shading, material gloss) more linearly than contrastive or masked-image features, because generation requires photometric competence that discriminative objectives can discard.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Self-supervised feature comparisons focus on semantic tasks (classification, segmentation, depth), while intrinsic-image properties are rarely used to differentiate pretraining objectives.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Generative pretraining preserves photometric factors as linearly decodable structure, whereas invariance-based objectives explicitly or implicitly suppress them, producing a measurable objective-dependent gap on intrinsics probes.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Linear probes for albedo/shading separation on public intrinsics benchmarks will show diffusion features beating a strong contrastive baseline by at least 15% relative error reduction; kill if the gap is under 5% relative or the ordering flips.
why_important: It would define which downstream families (relighting, material understanding, photometric stereo) should default to generative backbones, on mechanistic rather than leaderboard grounds.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Feature comparisons on intrinsics decomposition across pretraining objectives with matched encoders appear rare or absent.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Freeze three backbones (diffusion, contrastive, masked-autoencoder) of comparable scale, train small linear/convex heads on a public intrinsics dataset, and compare held-out decomposition error.
main_risk: Public intrinsics ground truth is small and partly synthetic, so conclusions may hinge on benchmark idiosyncrasies rather than the objective-level claim.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Backbone choice is assumed to matter mainly through scale and data, with the pretraining objective a second-order detail for dense tasks.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Masked-image models also reconstruct pixels and may retain photometric structure just as well, nullifying the generative-versus-discriminative dichotomy.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Frozen-feature probing on public intrinsics data across three public checkpoints is a single-GPU, roughly one-day experiment.

one_line_idea: Depth structure readable from image-diffusion features reflects genuinely 3D-consistent knowledge rather than 2D shading heuristics, testable by randomizing photometric cues and checking cross-view probe consistency.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Monocular depth can be probed from text-to-image diffusion features, but whether this reflects learned 3D structure or exploitable 2D cues (position in frame, shading, texture gradients) is unresolved.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A nontrivial fraction of depth information in diffusion features survives photometric-cue randomization and remains consistent across viewpoints of the same scene, indicating internal 3D structure beyond monocular heuristics.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Under stylization/relighting perturbations that destroy shading cues, depth-probe accuracy will retain at least 60% of its clean value, and cross-view depth-probe agreement on multi-view public scenes will exceed a chance-matched baseline by 25% or more; kill if either margin is missed.
why_important: It adjudicates the 'generative models learn 3D' claim with a concrete falsifiable protocol instead of qualitative renders, informing whether diffusion backbones are trustworthy for geometry tasks.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Depth probing of diffusion features exists; a cue-randomization plus cross-view consistency falsification design appears unreported.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Probe depth from diffusion features on a public RGB-D set, re-evaluate under controlled relighting/stylization of inputs, and separately measure cross-view consistency of probed depth on public multi-view scenes.
main_risk: Stylization perturbations also shift inputs off-distribution, confounding cue removal with domain shift; a discriminative-backbone control is required.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Enthusiasts assert generative models 'understand 3D'; skeptics say all monocular depth is cue exploitation; neither side runs cue-ablated multi-view consistency tests.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Depth probes may collapse entirely under cue randomization, revealing the 3D story to be shading heuristics all the way down.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Probing plus perturbation re-evaluation on public RGB-D and multi-view data is about 1-2 days on one GPU with public checkpoints.

one_line_idea: Conditional denoisers queried with a null prompt produce semantically richer features than genuinely unconditional models of matched scale, because text conditioning during training organizes the internal representation even when unused at inference.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Most diffusion-feature work extracts features from text-conditional models with an empty prompt and implicitly treats this as an unconditional representation.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Training-time text conditioning acts as an auxiliary supervision signal that structures intermediate features; a truly unconditional model trained on the same images will show systematically weaker semantic probes than the null-prompted conditional model.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] At matched architecture, data, and training compute, null-prompted conditional features will beat unconditional-model features by at least 4 points on a fixed semantic probe suite; kill if the gap is under 1.5 points.
why_important: It quantifies how much of the celebrated 'diffusion representation' actually comes from language supervision rather than the generative objective, redirecting credit and future pretraining design.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Conditional-versus-unconditional representational comparisons at matched budgets appear absent; the community compares across incomparable public checkpoints.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train paired small-scale diffusion models on a public captioned dataset, one text-conditional and one unconditional, matching everything else, then run the probe suite on both at several noise levels.
main_risk: Small-scale captioned training may under-represent the effect present at web scale, giving a false negative for the regime people care about.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Feature quality is attributed to the diffusion objective itself; the null-prompt convention is treated as a harmless implementation detail.
why_it_might_be_wrong: If conditioning pathways are effectively bypassed at null prompt, the two models may be representationally identical and the language-credit story evaporates.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two paired trainings at CIFAR/CC3M-small scale (roughly 2-4 GPU-days total on a single A100 with public data) plus probing.

family_fingerprint.manipulated_variable: presence of text conditioning during training

one_line_idea: Multi-timestep diffusion feature ensembles are mostly redundant: the timestep-feature stack has low effective rank, and a single well-chosen timestep plus a linear map recovers nearly all probe performance.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Diffusion-feature pipelines often ensemble features across several timesteps and layers, multiplying inference cost, on the assumption that different timesteps contribute complementary information.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Across timesteps, features are approximately linear transforms of a shared low-dimensional semantic core, so multi-timestep aggregation adds little beyond noise averaging.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] A probe on single best-timestep features plus a learned linear projection will come within 2 points of the full multi-timestep ensemble on a fixed probe suite, and CKA between timestep features will exceed 0.8 in the semantic band; kill if the ensemble advantage exceeds 5 points.
why_important: If redundancy holds, diffusion-as-backbone costs drop by the ensemble factor (often 3-10 denoiser passes), materially changing feasibility for dense-prediction deployment.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Ensembling is adopted from empirical gains in papers; an effective-rank analysis of the timestep-feature tensor with a pre-registered equivalence margin appears missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Compute features at 8 timesteps on a probe dataset, measure cross-timestep CKA and stacked-feature effective rank, then compare single-timestep-plus-projection probes against full ensembles.
main_risk: Redundancy may hold for classification-style probes but fail for dense boundary-sensitive tasks, splitting the conclusion by task family.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] More timesteps are assumed to see different abstraction levels and hence to be complementary.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Published ensemble gains may reflect genuine frequency-band complementarity (coarse layout at high noise, texture at low noise) that no single timestep carries.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Feature extraction and probing on a 10k-image public set is a sub-day single-GPU experiment with public checkpoints.

one_line_idea: Diffusion transformers develop high-norm 'register-like' tokens analogous to those in supervised ViTs, and these tokens store global photometric/style state whose deletion selectively breaks style while sparing layout.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] High-norm outlier tokens ('registers') are documented in discriminative ViTs, but whether generative DiT-style denoisers develop the same phenomenon, and what those tokens hold, is unexamined.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Generative training also induces high-norm aggregate tokens, but their content differs: they buffer global appearance statistics (palette, illumination, style) needed for globally coherent synthesis, rather than classification-relevant summaries.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Ablating the top-norm 1% of tokens mid-generation will change global style metrics (color histograms, texture statistics) by at least 3x more than layout metrics (object placement via off-the-shelf detection on outputs); kill if style and layout degrade proportionally within 1.5x.
why_important: It maps a known interpretability phenomenon onto generators, yields a concrete handle for training-free style control, and tests whether register formation is objective-dependent.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Registers are studied in discriminative ViTs; a generative-DiT register census with causal ablation of content type appears novel.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Scan token norms across layers/timesteps of a public DiT-based generator, identify outlier tokens, ablate or transplant them between generations, and quantify style-versus-layout deltas on generated batches.
main_risk: Token transplants may destabilize sampling entirely, producing garbage that measures nothing about content specialization.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Register tokens are seen as a quirk of discriminative ViT training; generative models are not expected to need them.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Denoisers have per-pixel outputs and skip connections that may remove the pressure to buffer global state in tokens at all.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Norm census plus ablation on a few hundred generations is a sub-day single-GPU experiment on public DiT checkpoints.

family_fingerprint.measurement_family: style vs layout statistics of generations

one_line_idea: Perception heads trained on one diffusion backbone transfer to a different diffusion backbone through a single linear adapter, indicating a shared 'generative representation geometry' across independently trained models.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Every new diffusion checkpoint (versions, retrains, different labs) currently requires retraining downstream perception heads from scratch, and cross-model representational compatibility is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Diffusion models trained on similar data converge to representations that are equivalent up to a linear map, so frozen heads plus a cheap adapter recover most cross-model transfer performance.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] A linear adapter fit on 1% of task data will recover at least 90% of the target-backbone's native head performance for segmentation/depth probes; kill if recovery is below 70% or requires nonlinear adapters to reach it.
why_important: Linear cross-model portability would decouple perception-head investment from generator churn and constitutes evidence for a convergent-representation law in generative models.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Representational convergence is studied across discriminative networks; a head-portability protocol across generative denoisers appears untested.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train dense-prediction heads on backbone A features, fit linear adapters from backbone B features to backbone A feature space on a small paired image set, and evaluate the frozen head on adapted features.
main_risk: Different latent VAEs between model families may break spatial alignment in ways no linear map fixes, confounding the geometry claim with tokenization mismatch.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Heads are assumed backbone-specific; nobody expects frozen heads to survive a backbone swap.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Convergence results in the literature concern coarse similarity metrics, which can be high while task-relevant fine structure remains incompatible.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Head training plus adapter fitting on public dense benchmarks across two public checkpoints is roughly 1-2 GPU-days on a single GPU.

one_line_idea: Generative pretraining specifically resolves symmetric-part ambiguity in semantic correspondence (left/right paws, wheels), predicting a large margin over discriminative features exactly on symmetry-confusable pairs and near-parity elsewhere.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Correspondence benchmarks average over all keypoint pairs, and reported diffusion-feature advantages are aggregate, leaving unexplained where the generative advantage actually comes from.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because generation requires globally consistent part assignment (a left wheel must stay left across the image), diffusion features carry global side/orientation context that discriminative local features lack; the advantage concentrates on symmetry-confusable keypoints.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Stratifying a public correspondence benchmark into symmetry-confusable versus unambiguous keypoints will show diffusion features reducing symmetry-flip errors by at least 30% relative to a matched discriminative baseline, while unambiguous-pair accuracy differs by under 5% relative; kill if the advantage is uniform across strata.
why_important: It converts a leaderboard delta into a mechanism (global consistency from generative training), guiding when practitioners should pay diffusion-feature inference costs.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Symmetry-flip stratification of correspondence errors by pretraining objective appears unpublished.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Label symmetry-confusable keypoint pairs on an existing public benchmark, evaluate diffusion and discriminative features, and compare error decompositions.
main_risk: Symmetry-confusable subsets are small, so confidence intervals may be too wide without extra annotation effort.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Diffusion-feature correspondence gains are attributed to generally 'richer' features rather than any specific relational capability.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The gains may instead come from higher feature resolution or ensemble effects that stratification will not isolate.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Stratified re-evaluation of existing public benchmarks with two feature families is a sub-day single-GPU analysis.

one_line_idea: Generative depth estimators fine-tuned from image diffusion models inherit a photometric prior that fails predictably on non-photorealistic inputs, locating the boundary of the 'repurpose a generator' recipe.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Fine-tuning text-to-image diffusion models into dense predictors (e.g., affine-invariant depth) is an established recipe, but where its advantage comes from and where it breaks are characterized only anecdotally.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The recipe's advantage is a photometric-realism prior; on inputs violating natural image statistics (line drawings, scientific visualizations, flat-shaded renders) generative depth models will degrade more than discriminatively pretrained depth models of matched in-domain accuracy.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On a matched-pairs protocol (photo vs non-photorealistic depiction of the same geometry), generative-prior depth error will increase at least 2x more than the discriminative baseline's increase; kill if degradations are within 25% relative of each other.
why_important: Teams are adopting generator-derived dense predictors broadly; a validated failure-boundary law tells them when the prior helps versus actively misleads.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Comparisons focus on photo benchmarks; a controlled depiction-style stress protocol contrasting pretraining priors appears missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Assemble photo/render/drawing triplets of identical scenes from public synthetic sources with ground-truth depth, evaluate both model families, and compare degradation ratios.
main_risk: Style transfer between depiction types also changes low-level statistics that affect both families, requiring careful matched-difficulty construction.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Generative initialization is assumed to give broadly better zero-shot robustness, full stop.
why_it_might_be_wrong: The generative prior may encode geometry abstractly enough to survive depiction shifts, in which case the recipe is even stronger than believed.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Evaluation-only study on public depth checkpoints plus synthetic scenes: under one day on a single GPU.

one_line_idea: Image generators know occluded shape: diffusion features support amodal (completed-shape) segmentation probes far above discriminative features, because generation requires representing whole objects before occlusion.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Amodal completion is hard for standard perception stacks trained on visible-pixel labels, and current amodal methods rely on specialized supervision.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] To synthesize plausible occlusion scenes, generative models internally represent complete object shape; linear probes on diffusion features will predict occluded object extent substantially better than probes on discriminative features with identical heads and data.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On public amodal benchmarks, diffusion-feature probes will beat matched discriminative-feature probes by at least 8 points amodal IoU on heavily occluded instances; kill if the margin is under 3 points.
why_important: A validated amodal advantage would open a cheap route to occlusion-aware perception (robotics grasping, driving) without amodal-specific pretraining.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Diffusion features are probed for visible-region tasks; systematic amodal probing with occlusion-stratified analysis appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train identical lightweight amodal-mask heads on frozen diffusion versus discriminative features using a public amodal dataset, stratify results by occlusion fraction.
main_risk: Amodal ground truth is partly annotator convention, capping measurable differences between any two feature families.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Amodal ability is assumed to require explicit amodal supervision or video; static generative pretraining is not credited with it.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Generators may handle occlusion purely at the pixel level during synthesis without maintaining reusable object-complete representations.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Frozen-feature head training on a public amodal dataset: about one day on one GPU.

one_line_idea: Diffusion-classifier accuracy is bottlenecked by noise-sample variance rather than model knowledge, so paired-noise variance reduction closes most of the gap to discriminative readouts at a fraction of the usual inference cost.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Classification via conditional diffusion likelihood estimates (diffusion classifiers) trails discriminative heads and needs many noise samples per class, which is attributed to generative models simply being worse classifiers.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The class-conditional loss differences that drive the decision are small relative to per-noise-sample variance; sharing identical noise draws across classes and antithetic sampling shrink the estimator variance enough to reveal substantially higher underlying accuracy.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Variance-reduced estimation at a fixed budget of 32 denoiser calls per image will recover at least half of the accuracy gap between a naive 32-call diffusion classifier and its 512-call ceiling; kill if the recovery is under 20% of that gap.
why_important: If the bottleneck is estimator variance, generative classifiers become practical zero-shot evaluators of what generators know, and 'generative models are bad classifiers' needs rewriting as 'naive estimators are bad'.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Paired-noise evaluation is used in some evaluation contexts; a systematic variance-decomposition study of diffusion classifiers appears missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Implement naive versus paired/antithetic estimators on a public text-to-image checkpoint over a class-balanced public subset, plot accuracy versus number of denoiser calls for both, and compare convergence.
main_risk: Variance reduction cannot fix systematic likelihood biases (e.g., class-dependent contour lengths), which may dominate for fine-grained classes.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The gap is read as generative pretraining encoding less discriminative information.
why_it_might_be_wrong: If bias rather than variance dominates, the recovery will be negligible and the pessimistic reading stands.
fastest_falsification_experiment: A few thousand images with tens of denoiser calls each on one GPU: about one day with public checkpoints and data.

one_line_idea: Cross-attention localization in text-to-image models collapses selectively for relational prompts: attention maps localize single objects well but misassign attributes in two-object scenes at a rate predictable from token co-occurrence statistics.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Cross-attention maps are widely reused as free open-vocabulary localizers, but their failure structure is folklore rather than quantified.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Attention-map localization is reliable exactly when prompt tokens map to visually distinctive regions independently, and breaks when attribute binding is required, with error rate rising with training-corpus co-occurrence between the attributes and both objects.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On generated two-object scenes with swapped attributes, token-attribution maps will assign the attribute to the wrong object in at least 25% of cases while single-object localization stays above 85% pointing-game accuracy; kill if relational and single-object accuracy differ by under 10 points.
why_important: Dozens of pipelines mine attention maps for grounding; a quantified reliability boundary determines when that shortcut corrupts downstream labels.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Attribute-binding failures are known for generation quality; their signature specifically in attention-based localization appears uncharacterized.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Generate controlled two-object attribute-swap prompts, extract token attention maps, score object and attribute assignment against automatically checkable layouts, stratify by corpus co-occurrence estimates.
main_risk: Attention maps depend on layer/timestep aggregation choices, so conclusions must be shown stable across the standard extraction recipes.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Cross-attention is treated as a serviceable free localizer whose errors are unstructured noise.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Localization may fail more broadly (even single objects) once evaluated beyond cherry-picked classes, making the relational story too generous.
fastest_falsification_experiment: A few thousand controlled generations plus automated scoring: under one day on a single GPU.
